title: Claude Shannon, Ilya Prigogine & Carl Woese (1916–2001 / 1917–2003 / 1928–2012) — Boolean Relay Logic & the Bit, Far-From-Equilibrium Dissipative Structures, and Reading 16S Ribosomal RNA to Discover Archaea

teenKit.tldr: Life isn't just a static collection of animal parts; it's a high-tech engine driven by digital logic, continuous energy flow, and ancient molecular memories.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how living cells process data and energy transforms everything from how we fight drug-resistant diseases to how we build biological computers.
keyTakeaways: Claude Shannon proved that the basic 'yes/no' logic of electrical switches could be used to process any form of information, inventing the foundation of the digital world.
Ilya Prigogine showed that living things survive by constantly consuming energy to fight off chaos, existing as stable whirlpools far from chemical equilibrium.
Carl Woese ignored traditional visual classifications and used molecular genetic signatures to discover Archaea, completely redrawing the tree of life.

vocab.meaning: A system of electrical switches that makes true-or-false decisions, serving as the blueprint for all modern computing.
An organized system that stays stable only by constantly using up outside energy, just like a living cell or a spinning hurricane.
An ancient molecular sequence found in all cells that acts like a built-in historical family tree for every living thing.
A massive, distinct domain of single-celled microscopic life that looks like bacteria but is genetically as different from them as we are.

quiz.question: What breakthrough did Claude Shannon achieve in his famous 1937 master's thesis?
options: He invented the very first smartphone screen.
He connected telephone lines using barbed wire in Michigan.
He proved that electrical relay switches could perform logical math.
He decoded the chemical structure of DNA.
quiz.explanation: Shannon realized that true/false logical statements could be directly mapped onto open/closed electrical circuits.

quiz.question: How do living systems survive according to Ilya Prigogine's physics of open systems?
options: By sealing themselves off completely to prevent any energy loss.
By continuously consuming external energy to fight off internal chaos.
By reaching a dead state of complete chemical balance.
By mimicking the digital logic of silicon microchips.
quiz.explanation: Life is a far-from-equilibrium structure that maintains its internal order by constantly dissipating energy from its environment.

quiz.question: Why did Carl Woese's discovery of Archaea face decades of skepticism from traditional biologists?
options: He relied on computer software instead of microscope images.
Archaea looked identical to standard plants under a lens.
He refused to publish his data in scientific journals.
His molecular classification shattered the neat visual sorting boxes of traditional biology.
quiz.explanation: Woese used molecular sequencing rather than physical appearance, proving that visual categories fail to capture the true tree of life.
